title: C4092 — Left rear height sensor connector
introduction:
I use this reference to connect the left rear height sensor’s identity with its connector drawing and circuit map. Think of the drawing as a seating chart: the cavity label tells you where to look in the table, and the Function column explains that circuit’s role.

Start with the connector description, then find the harness heading and drawing. Match a printed cavity label to its Cavity row and read across that row. This keeps the suspension-position sensor connection distinct from the control-module connections marked with opposite polarity signs. The pigtail table provides a separate service-parts lookup.

This page teaches identification and reference reading. It does not establish the physical viewing direction, access method, electrical test conditions or replacement procedure. Gauge conventions and the meanings of Box, Size and Used codes are not defined here; retain those entries without turning them into tool sizes, wire-selection advice or test results.

edits.why: I use the housing detail above the horizontal cavity row as a landmark within the drawing. Read the printed cavity labels rather than assuming they increase from left to right. That establishes how to navigate this illustration without claiming which side of a physical connector you would be viewing. The table below associates the drawing with its Fpn and harness entry.
